req.title: Create schema on startup
req.statement: The system shall create the tasks table via SQLAlchemy metadata at application startup.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-024 requires that the tasks table is created via SQLAlchemy metadata at application startup. The key observable effect is that the app is reachable (HTTP 2xx on root) and the tasks endpoint is functional immediately after import — no manual migration step needed. Tests cover: (1) positive: app starts and root returns 200 with exact payload, proving startup completed; (2) positive EP: GET /tasks returns the 20 pre-loaded rows proving the table exists and is queryable; (3) negative: verifying that a bad route returns 404 not 500, proving the app is up but the route doesn't exist (server error would indicate startup failure); (4) boundary BVA: the tasks table supports insert+retrieve of a task with a 1-char title (min_length=1) immediately after startup, proving schema is fully operational; (5) STC: app lifecycle — import triggers create_all, then POST then GET confirms round-trip through the schema created at startup.

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_root_returns_200_with_exact_payload():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert body["message"] == "Welcome to Task Manager API"
    assert body["docs"] == "/docs"
    assert body["version"] == "1.0.0"
    assert len(body) == 3

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_tasks_table_exists_and_has_preloaded_rows():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/tasks/")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    tasks = r.json()
    assert isinstance(tasks, list)
    assert len(tasks) == 20
    ids = {t["id"] for t in tasks}
    assert 1 in ids
    assert 20 in ids
    first = next(t for t in tasks if t["id"] == 1)
    assert first["title"] == "Read chapter 5"
    assert first["completed"] == True
    assert "created_at" in first

expected: Response contains id=21, correct title, completed=False
GET returns HTTP 200 with same task data
trace: R-TASK-024: schema created at startup enables full CRUD lifecycle
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_schema_supports_create_and_retrieve_task():
    client = TestClient(app)
    payload = {"title": "Startup schema test task", "completed": False}
    r = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    created = r.json()
    assert created["id"] == 21
    assert created["title"] == "Startup schema test task"
    assert created["completed"] == False
    assert "created_at" in created
    task_id = created["id"]
    r2 = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    fetched = r2.json()
    assert fetched["id"] == 21
    assert fetched["title"] == "Startup schema test task"
    assert fetched["completed"] == False

def test_startup_schema_boundary_max_title_length_100_chars():
    client = TestClient(app)

    assert r_valid.status_code == 201
    body = r_valid.json()

    assert body["id"] == 21

tests.name: test_startup_completed_filter_returns_correct_subset
preconditions: Pre-loaded rows: ids 1,2,3,9,15,19 are completed=True (6 rows)
expected: completed=true returns exactly 6 items all with completed=True
completed=false returns exactly 14 items all with completed=False
trace: R-TASK-024: schema created at startup; filter query proves table is queryable with correct data
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_completed_filter_returns_correct_subset():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r_true = client.get("/tasks/?completed=true")
    assert r_true.status_code == 200
    completed_tasks = r_true.json()
    assert len(completed_tasks) == 6
    assert all(t["completed"] == True for t in completed_tasks)
    completed_ids = {t["id"] for t in completed_tasks}
    assert completed_ids == {1, 2, 3, 9, 15, 19}
    r_false = client.get("/tasks/?completed=false")
    assert r_false.status_code == 200
    incomplete_tasks = r_false.json()
    assert len(incomplete_tasks) == 14
    assert all(t["completed"] == False for t in incomplete_tasks)
    assert len(completed_tasks) + len(incomplete_tasks) == 20
